title: npm global installs are exempt from the lockfile check only when fully standalone
answers: npm install -g flagged as mutable lockfile install
global npm install false positive in workflow policy
why does npm install --global fail the lockfile policy
npm install with -g and chained commands bypasses policy
body:
Symptom: a workflow step doing a global npm install (e.g. `npm install -g eslint`) is reported as a mutable lockfile install, or a local install chained with a global one escapes the check.
Root cause: the lockfile exemption in .github/policy.rego matched a global flag anywhere on the command line, so unrelated -g/--global tokens or chained commands exempted a local install.
Fix pattern: exempt only a complete standalone `npm install` command whose -g or --global flag appears on either side of plain package arguments; evaluate each command separately rather than the whole run line.
Constraints: chained commands (`&&`, `;`) and unrelated flags such as `echo --global` must not qualify for the exemption; the exemption is for global installs only, so local installs still require a lockfile.
applies: Lockfile and npm install checks in .github/policy.rego.
says: Build pipeline security policy incorrectly flags global tool installations as missing lockfiles
Workflow run check fails with lockfile error when installing global packages
Chained package installation commands slip past automated repository policy checks
Exempt standalone global tool setup from workflow lockfile compliance checks
search: In .github/policy.rego, workflow lockfile checks must exempt global npm install commands only when they are complete and standalone. The exemption requires -g or --global to appear on either side of plain package arguments, evaluating each command separately rather than across the entire run line. Chained commands using && or ; and unrelated tokens like echo --global must not qualify, ensuring local installs still require a lockfile.
